hints: Remember what the alkaline iodine test is really looking for, the iodoform reaction only works with two very specific groupings.
Check each structure for a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, only two of the four have one of these.
For the ones that pass the iodine test, look for a carbon with four different groups attached, that chiral centre would mean optical isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

A positive test means a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$. It is given by ethanal, methyl ketones and related secondary alcohols.

The rule to use is:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ or } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \text{ gives positive iodoform test}$$

**Apply the test to the four compounds**

Look for those two groups in each structure.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so positive. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$ also has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so positive. The other two have neither $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ nor $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so they are negative.

**Check for optical isomerism**

Optical isomerism needs a chiral centre, a carbon joined to four different groups.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$ has $\text{CH(OH)}$ joined to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{COCH}_3$, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ has only $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{C=O}$ and $\text{CH}_2$ groups, no carbon has four different groups, so it is achiral.

**Combine both conditions**

We need positive iodine test AND no chiral centre.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ satisfies both, so it is the answer.

options.A: Contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, a methyl ketone, so gives $\text{CHI}_3$ yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine. It has no chiral centre because the carbons are $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{C=O}$, $\text{CH}_2$, $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so it does not show optical isomerism. Meets both conditions.
options.B: Structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$. It has neither $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ nor $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so iodoform test is negative. It also has a chiral centre at $\text{CH(OH)}$ joined to $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CHO}$, so it does show optical isomerism. Fails both conditions.
options.C: Structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$. It does give a positive iodoform test due to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, which is a common trap. However the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon is chiral (attached to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{COCH}_3$), so it does show optical isomerism and fails the second condition.
options.D: Structure is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)CHO}$. The central carbon has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so it is achiral and shows no optical isomerism. However it has neither $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ nor $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so the iodoform test is negative. Fails the first condition.
